name: a_ai_capex
prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Monday October 5, 2026. Topic: AI capex & cloud.

Window: Friday October 2, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Monday October 5, 2026 12:20 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. This spans 2 non-trading day(s): news published on those days (e.g. Saturday and Sunday) is in scope and often the most important. Anything published after 12:20 ET on Monday October 5, 2026 is out of scope.

FIND
Hyperscaler capex estimates and commentary (with firm/analyst name), AI cloud and compute deals ($ value, term), data-center projects, delays or cancellations, AI financing (bonds, converts, private credit), OpenAI/Anthropic/xAI funding and compute commitments, GPU cloud pricing.

Run multiple searches with different phrasings and dates. Prefer primary sources and wire services
(Reuters, Bloomberg, AP, CNBC, WSJ, MarketWatch, Barron's, Investopedia, company press releases, SEC
EDGAR, BLS/BEA/Census/Fed releases, FDA). For every item give the latest status as of the cutoff.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or topic:

## TICKER or Topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

Category: pick from AI Compute · Memory & Interconnect · Optical & Photonics · Chip Equipment · Fab & Foundry · Wireless & Mobile · Analog & Mixed-Signal · Power & Wide-Bandgap · Test & Advanced Packaging · Specialty Materials & IP Licensing · Quantum Computing · EdgeAI · Semiconductors · AI Infrastructure · Software & SaaS · Internet & Platforms · Communications & Networking, or Macro / Commodities / Geopolitics / Crypto / Calendar /
Pharma / Energy / Retail, or a concise sector name. Bold tickers.

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## **AI Infrastructure** — Hyperscaler capex and financing

- Goldman Sachs estimated AI-related debt issuance reached nearly **$500 billion** in 2026 by early August; about **40%** was issued directly by hyperscalers including Amazon, Microsoft and Alphabet. (R&D World, Oct. 2, 2026, 20:52 ET)

- Alphabet raised its 2026 capital-expenditure outlook in July to **$195 billion–$205 billion**, from **$180 billion–$190 billion**. (R&D World, Oct. 2, 2026, 20:52 ET)

- Amazon’s expected 2026 cash capital expenditure was reported at approximately **$220 billion**, **$20 billion** above its prior plan; the increase was attributed to higher memory prices and expansion of AI data-center infrastructure. (R&D World, Oct. 2, 2026, 20:52 ET)

- Microsoft’s projected 2026 capex was reported at approximately **$175 billion**, down from about **$190 billion** after a shift from finance leases to operating leases; the report said the accounting change did not alter the company’s investment plans. (R&D World, Oct. 2, 2026, 20:52 ET)

- Andreessen Horowitz estimated 2026 capital expenditure by Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle at approximately **$780 billion**, compared with **$416 billion in 2025**, and forecast more than **$1 trillion annually from 2027**. (Matterfact, Oct. 1, 2026, 21:24 ET)

- Goldman Sachs and other estimates cited in an Oct. 4 analysis put combined 2026 hyperscaler capital expenditure at approximately **$940 billion** and projected more than **$1.3 trillion in 2027**. (IEEE ComSoc Technology Blog, Oct. 4, 2026, 19:01 ET)

- The same analysis cited projected 2026 debt issuance of **$220 billion–$250 billion or more** by Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle, with total AI-related debt issuance potentially reaching **$570 billion**. (IEEE ComSoc Technology Blog, Oct. 4, 2026, 19:01 ET)

## **AVGO** — AI Compute / AI financing

- Broadcom agreed to provide Anthropic up to **$42 billion** through convertible notes to help finance Anthropic’s infrastructure spending, according to Anthropic’s IPO prospectus reviewed by Reuters. (Reuters, Oct. 2, 2026; publish time not provided)

- Anthropic committed to a **$125.2 billion, five-year** lease of Broadcom-built TPU capacity; the financing would cover approximately one-third of that commitment. (Reuters, Oct. 2, 2026; publish time not provided)

- The convertible notes could be converted into Anthropic equity over five years; Broadcom could bring in a financing partner, and no notes were expected to be sold before Anthropic completed its IPO. (The Signal, Oct. 2, 2026, 10:06 ET)

- Bloomberg reported that Broadcom’s banking syndicate was assembling approximately **$60 billion** of chip financing for Anthropic and other companies, including **$42 billion** of senior secured debt and **$18 billion** of junior debt led by Blackstone. [report] (R&D World, Oct. 2, 2026, 20:21 ET)

## **Anthropic** — AI Compute / AI financing

- Anthropic’s IPO prospectus disclosed a **$125.2 billion, five-year** commitment to lease TPU computing capacity from Broadcom. (Reuters, Oct. 2, 2026; publish time not provided)

- Anthropic disclosed a plan to spend approximately **$518 billion** on cloud and computing infrastructure over the next decade. (Artificial Prism, Oct. 3, 2026, 09:10 ET)

- Anthropic had agreed to obtain approximately **3.5 gigawatts** of TPU-based compute through Broadcom beginning in **2027**. (AI Daily Insights, Oct. 2, 2026, updated Oct. 4, 2026, 20:05 ET)

## **OpenAI** — AI Compute / AI financing

- SoftBank and Nvidia each made a final **$10 billion** payment, completing **$20 billion** of remaining commitments to OpenAI’s March funding round; the payments arrived on **October 1, 2026**. [report] (AI Daily Insights, Oct. 2, 2026, updated Oct. 3, 2026, 00:43 ET)

- OpenAI’s March funding round valued the company at approximately **$852 billion post-money**; Amazon’s **$50 billion** commitment had been completed in July, while SoftBank and Nvidia funded their commitments in stages. [report] (AI Daily Insights, Oct. 2, 2026, updated Oct. 3, 2026, 00:43 ET)

- OpenAI was reported to be discussing a private pre-IPO round of more than **$30 billion** at a valuation above **$1.4 trillion**; the talks were described as early-stage. [rumor][report] (Michael Parekh, Oct. 3, 2026, 11:34 ET)

- Oracle reportedly signed a **$300 billion, five-year** cloud agreement with OpenAI beginning in **2027**, covering approximately **4.5 gigawatts** of computing capacity. [report; direct cause dated September 2025] (R&D World, Oct. 2, 2026, 20:52 ET)

## **TSLA / SpaceX-related AI compute** — AI Compute

- Anthropic reportedly agreed to pay approximately **$1.25 billion per month** through **May 2029** for compute across xAI’s Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 sites; the reported arrangement involved approximately **220,000 GPUs** and a **90-day termination clause**. [report] (Artificial Prism, Oct. 3, 2026, 14:47 ET)

- Google reportedly secured approximately **110,000 GPUs** from xAI’s Colossus 2 for approximately **$920 million per month** through **June 2029**, with service beginning in **October 2026**. [report] (Artificial Prism, Oct. 3, 2026, 14:47 ET)

- Anthropic was reported to have committed approximately **$84.5 billion** for Nvidia-powered capacity associated with SpaceX and xAI. [report] (Observer, Oct. 1, 2026, updated Oct. 2, 2026, 10:19 ET)

## **AI Infrastructure** — Data centers and cloud capacity

- Oracle had approximately **$137 billion** of debt and leases, and S&P estimated that about **half of Oracle’s $638 billion backlog** was associated with OpenAI. [report] (R&D World, Oct. 2, 2026, 20:52 ET)

- Microsoft allocated approximately **two-thirds** of its fourth-quarter capex to short-lived assets including CPUs and GPUs, with the remainder directed to data-center infrastructure. (R&D World, Oct. 2, 2026, 20:52 ET)

- Alphabet reported that approximately **60%** of its capital spending was directed to servers and approximately **40%** to data centers and networking equipment. (R&D World, Oct. 2, 2026, 20:52 ET)

## **Memory & Interconnect** — AI infrastructure supply

- A market analysis citing Nvidia commentary said cloud-company capex could grow by approximately **70% in 2027**, following comparable growth by the four largest cloud companies in 2026. (IEEE ComSoc Technology Blog, Oct. 4, 2026, 19:01 ET)

- The same analysis cited a forecast that cloud capital expenditure could rise by approximately **50% in 2027**, below the approximately **70%** growth scenario attributed to more bullish industry forecasts. (IEEE ComSoc Technology Blog, Oct. 4, 2026, 19:01 ET)
